label: Recommended architecture: keep Product Owner as the workflow owner for source classification, flow semantics, and FigJam-only delivery, while routing explicitly requested board reads and writes to an embedded mcp-figma tool packet; this matches Moneybird’s default-workflow/non-default-tool split and avoids making a low-level CLI own the product workflow. For Figma links, parse fileKey/nodeId and request scoped design data or referenced images only after live MCP tool/schema discovery; the manual lists the MCP as file/node retrieval and image download, while FigJam creation uses the CLI’s fj write verbs. The manuals document screenshot-url for website captures into Figma but do not establish arbitrary local screenshot OCR/import, so treat screenshot extraction as an unresolved adapter spike. Product docs should preserve claim-level current/approved/proposal/retired/unknown status and stop composition when authority does not resolve a conflict. Carry over flow semantics—distinct node types, top-down direction, decisions with at most three exits, labeled branches, and restrained density—but implement the geometry with FigJam-native objects: preserve orthogonal routing and readable, non-overlapping, unobscured connectors while translating SVG-specific masks, pixel gaps, bridges, and grid enforcement into verified FigJam equivalents. The parent spec forbids HTML/SVG output, so validators and export contracts for those formats do not carry over. Vendor the mcp-figma subtree as a clearly owned copy plus a narrow Product Owner FigJam adapter; keep the shared .skilled source authoritative and sync accepted improvements through an explicit diff/patch review before re-vendoring, since Product Owner’s parity note governs only its hand-written Claude Project mirrors and keeps no manifest, lock, or checksum ledger. Product Owner’s current manifest is a standalone single-mode manifest, so the vendor package should not be mistaken for a hub registry. Build a thin Claude Code plugin around the installed figma-ds-cli rather than bundling Media Editor’s custom server; expose preflight/version/help, safe FigJam reads, explicit-target gated writes, and board read-back. Convert Product Owner to a Moneybird-style hub with its current workflow as the sole default workflow packet and mcp-figma as a non-default tool packet, then pin routes for explicit FigJam output intent, ordinary Figma UI feedback, negation, quoted tool names, and mixed inputs. Moneybird’s prefix-match, raw-negation, and corpus/live-model gaps show why gold-route replay, mutation guards, and live smoke must be separate gates. Sequence feasibility first, then vendor/sync, hub/router, flow engine, plugin, and integrated checks; Figma auth/rate limits, drifting @latest schemas, secrets, and output gating remain risks.
